subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value: A SLOT-COUNT SURPLUS IS A DECLARATION-COUNT SURPLUS, AND SLOTDIFF'S USE COUNTS -- NOT ITS EXCLUSIVE-PAIR SET -- ARE WHAT LOCATE IT. MWCC 1.2.5 gives every distinct declared local its own stack slot; it does NOT overlay two locals whose live ranges are disjoint. Therefore when our build has more slots than the target, the surplus is source-reachable by deleting declarations, and the target is telling you the original reused ONE variable where the reconstruction invented several. THE FINGERPRINT: a scratch array the original reused across sibling loops appears in the target as a SINGLE slot whose use count is the SUM of the uses, and in ours as N slots that PARTITION that same sum. In ProcessEffects the target's slot 104 carried 51 uses while our three corresponding vectors (an inner lightpos, an inner delta, an inner enemyDelta, plus a function-scope normal) split those uses across four separate slots; the exclusive-pair view merely said 21T/31O and named no cause, while the per-slot use counts named it immediately. Read the full map (slotdiff --all) and look for a target slot whose count is a near-sum of several of ours. THE TECHNIQUE THAT RESOLVES WHICH LOCAL IS WHICH: dump every address-take (addi rX,r1,N) from both sides in instruction order and pair them BY INSTRUCTION INDEX. On a large function the two streams stay within a few instructions of each other, so the pairing is unambiguous and yields a direct variable-correspondence table -- target slot S at index i is whatever our source passes at index i. That table is what distinguishes 'the same variable moved' from 'the original used a different variable here', and it is the only cheap way to tell them apart on a 2300-instruction body. CONFIRMED COROLLARY, AND THE TRAP: the fix is to stop WRITING to the surplus local, not merely to delete its declaration. Deleting a declaration that is still referenced changes the local count, which re-orders MWCC's whole pre-loop f64 constant-hoist block; in ProcessEffects that cost real 1741 -> 2163, measured twice with identical scores before and after four intervening improvements, so the alignment-sensitivity retry does not rescue it. Fold the surplus variable's USES onto the reused one first and let the declaration fall out; each such fold scored IMPROVED on its own, and one of them (a light-position vector folded onto hitpos) was worth 330 real lines by itself. WHY THE ORDINARY METRICS MISS ALL OF THIS: across the entire 412-line real improvement the instruction counts (T2309/O2304) and the opcode multiset (23 tokens) NEVER MOVED. Any classifier keyed on the multiset calls such a function finished. Corroborates claim.law.EN-ops-multiset-cannot-classify-a-residual-run-slotdiff-first.20260901.v1 and is governed by claim.law.stack-slots-descend-in-declaration-order.20260831.v1, which is what lets you PREDICT the landing slot: promoting a local to function scope at a chosen point in the declaration list places it at a computable address, and the prediction was confirmed to the exact use count (target 92:6/96:1/100:4 reproduced exactly). FREE EVIDENCE FIRST: the TU's own header comment above ProcessEffects listed the Xbox principal locals (mat/omat/pos/opos/dir/hitpos) and the target frame size 0x2f0; it both bounded the goal and showed which of our locals were invented. Four prior passes on this function did not read it.
